content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, it is critical to call 911 immediately. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your healthcare provider may recommend laboratory or medical tests, such as vaginal ultrasounds, hormone level assessments, or liver function tests, to monitor your condition and response to treatment. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health requirements. Common side effects of this medication may include redness or pain at the injection site, headache, mild nausea or stomach pain, and fatigue. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this medication may cause a condition called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), which can occur during or after treatment. In rare cases, severe OHSS can lead to a sudden buildup of fluid in the abdomen, chest, or heart area. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using ganirelix, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other products containing gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as latex, which could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, this treatment may increase the likelihood of multiple births. Discontinue use of this medication if you become pregnant, as it must not be used during pregnancy. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication due to potential risks to the infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away.
